points.description: States that a data member can be accessed by any/all member functions of the class (class-wide scope).
States that a local variable can only be accessed inside the member function that defines it (function-limited scope).
Makes a clear contrast between the two, i.e. data member scope is the whole class while local variable scope is a single function. Equivalent wording accepted.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if the contrast is only implied by separate descriptions without explicit comparison.
